html:
The Cabiyarí are a small Indigenous people of the Vaupés region of southeastern Colombia, living near the Apaporis river in the Amazon forest. Their language belongs to the Arawakan family, unlike those of most of their neighbours, who speak Tucanoan languages, such as the Makuna and the Cubeo.

Like other peoples of the region they live by gardening manioc, fishing and hunting, and marry across language lines. Few speakers of Cabiyarí remain. The area was hit by rubber collectors in the rubber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s.
